 Need help with winter heating bills? Here is who qualifies for energy assistance in Quad Cities 
 Eligible renters and homeowners can get assistance through LIHEAP 
 Eligible Iowa and Illinois renters and homeowners can get assistance through LIHEAP. By Cyle Dickens Published : Oct. 26, 2026 at 6:25 PM CDT | Updated : 15 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google DAVENPORT, Iowa (KWQC) - As winter approaches, what you pay to heat your home will depend largely on how you heat it.
 The U.S. Energy Information Administration projects natural gas and propane bills will dip slightly this winter thanks to strong inventories. But households heating with electricity can expect bills about 4% higher, and heating oil costs could run more than 20% higher than last winter.
 With groceries, rent and gas still straining budgets, many families are forced to choose which bill to pay first. For struggling households, help is available through the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, known as LIHEAP.
 What LIHEAP does 
 LIHEAP is a federally funded grant — it does not have to be paid back — that pays a portion of winter heating costs for eligible renters and homeowners. The amount is based on household income, household size, dwelling type and heating fuel.
 When to apply 
 Iowa: 
 Oct. 1: Households with an adult 60 or older, individuals with disabilities 
 Nov. 1: All other eligible households 
 Through April 30: first-come, first-served 
 Illinois: 
 Adults 60 and older, individuals with disabilities, families with children age 5 and under, and households facing disconnection 
 Nov. 1: All other eligible households 
 Through Aug. 13, 2027, or until funds run out 
 Income limits 
 Iowa: at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines:
 1 person: $31,920 
 2 people: $43,280 
 4 people: $66,000 
 Illinois: up to 300% of federal poverty guidelines for Ameren, ComEd, Nicor and Peoples Gas customers:
 1 person: $47,880 
 2 people: $64,920 
 4 people: $99,000 
 What to bring 
 Requirements vary by agency, but you will typically need to bring:
 Heating and electric bills from the last 30 days 
 30 days of income records for all household members 
 Social Security cards or ITINs for household members 
 Lease showing rent amount and whether heat is included, if you rent 
 Facing a shutoff? Contact both your utility provider and your local community action agency immediately to request emergency assistance, and be sure to mention your disconnection notice right away.
 Where to apply in the Quad Cities area 
 Iowa - Community Action of Eastern Iowa serves Scott, Clinton, Muscatine and Cedar counties. caeiowa.org | Call your county outreach office. State info: 515-281-3861
 Illinois - Project NOW serves Rock Island, Henry and Mercer counties. projectnow.org | helpillinoisfamilies.com | 1-833-711-0374
 Illinois - Tri-County Opportunities Council serves Whiteside, Carroll, Bureau, Lee, Ogle and surrounding counties tcochelps.org | 815-625-7830 or 800-323-5434
 Illinois - WIRC-Community Action Agency serves Knox, Hancock, Henderson, McDonough and Warren counties wirpc.org/liheap | Knox County (Galesburg): 309-837-5115 | Macomb: 309-837-2997
 Help beyond the bill 
 Weatherization: Free home efficiency upgrades through Iowa Weatherization Assistance and Illinois Home Weatherization Assistance Program (IHWAP) via your local Community Action agency 
 Utility hardship funds: MidAmerican I CARE (888-427-5632), Ameren Illinois assistance and Low-Income Discounts, Alliant Hometown Care, plus Budget Billing and payment plans 
 Local safety net: Salvation Army, St. Vincent de Paul, crisis and furnace repair funds through Community Action 
 Call 211 for referrals if you are unsure where to start. 
 Advocates urge families not to wait: Pick up the phone now, well before the coldest days of winter.
 Sources: U.S. Energy Information Administration Oct. 6 Winter Fuels Outlook 2026-27; Iowa Dept. of Health and Human Services; Illinois Dept. of Commerce and Economic Opportunity.
